messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—patronage is crumbling, but the military’s locked in, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet for now. People are talking, but no one’s moving yet, and the foreign embassies are the only ones sweating. We’re not out of the woods, but right now, the system’s holding—just don’t bet on it staying that way forever."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s not as solid as they want us to think. The memes, the soldiers chatting at checkpoints, the women in the market dropping names—it’s all small cracks, but they’re there. And if the foreign embassies are whispering warnings, that’s not a good sign. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. This could go either way."*"
Sender 3: "*"They’re holding the line for now, but the cracks are there—junior officials are still playing the game, the streets are humming with something unspoken, and even the money changers know the script is off. The question isn’t if the facade will hold, but how long they can keep pretending it’s not crumbling behind closed doors."*"
Sender 4: "*"They’re holding, but it’s not the calm before the storm—it’s the quiet after the first warning shot. The regime’s still got its moves, but the cracks are in the *how*, not the *what*: they’re buying time, not winning it."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the machine’s still running—same old incentives, same old shows of strength—but the gears are grinding louder than they used to. My cousin’s silence, the extra flights, the unit that ‘forgot’ its patrol… it’s not panic yet, but it’s the kind of quiet that makes you check your exits. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re not just confident—they’re *preparing* for something, and it’s not panic. The checkpoints are down, the inner circle’s growing, and even the streets are whispering the same thing: this isn’t a crackdown coming, it’s a *shift*. The question isn’t if it happens, but how hard we’ll hit the ground when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not ready, and neither are they."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the ship’s still afloat—no one’s panicking, but the crew’s keeping their cards close. The money’s moving, the uniforms are paid, and the streets are quiet, but the cracks are showing in the little things—garbage piles, delayed permits, my cousin’s silence. They’re holding it together for now, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—but it’s not the chaos we feared. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, no cracks in the walls, no panic in the ranks. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet. If we’re going to move, it can’t be on hope—it’s got to be on something real, and right now, the only thing real is that they’re not going anywhere soon."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the regime’s playing the long game—no cracks in the walls, just a lot of noise to keep us guessing. The real signal? They’re too busy tightening their grip to even bother pretending they’re worried."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation. The top is holding together for now, but the military’s just going through the motions, and people are starting to test the edges. The real question is whether this is the calm before the storm or just another round of the same old game. Either way, we need to be ready for either—because right now, the wind could blow in any direction."*"
Sender 11: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing: soldiers being shuffled around, the internet slowing down for no reason, even the black market acting like things might get easier soon. And that moment of silence at the meeting? Everyone knew exactly what it meant. They’re holding on tight, but the question isn’t *if* something gives—it’s *when* and *how hard*."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are holding for now—unified responses, contracts being signed, even the security folks acting like it’s business as usual—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The regime’s still got its foot on the gas, but the engine’s sputtering, and the question isn’t *if* something gives, it’s *when* and whether anyone’s ready to step in when it does."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the machine is still humming—no cracks in the gears, just the usual noise. The big players are all still in their seats, the money’s flowing where it’s supposed to, and even the street’s acting like nothing’s wrong. But that audit getting pulled? That’s the only thing that’s got me wondering—what did they *not* want us to see?"*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are showing—elites are playing nice, the streets are getting louder, and the money’s still moving, but the schools are on the brink. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but when—and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’re holding it together for now, but the seams are starting to show—empty posts, delayed responses, and that weird mix of tight credit and forced transparency. The streets are quiet, but not because people are happy—just because they’re too tired to fight. Keep your eyes open, but don’t panic. Yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re holding, but it’s not as smooth as they want us to think—someone got quietly cut loose, and the money’s still moving, but the teachers are starting to drag their feet. The streets are calm, but the top’s talking to itself more than to us. Not breaking yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 17: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but you can feel it. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the fixer who’s suddenly invisible, the security guys dragging their feet, the money slipping away like sand. People are talking more, but still in code—like they’re waiting to see who blinks first. The big question? Will anyone actually move when the moment comes—or will we all just keep pretending we don’t see it?"*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s showing its teeth in public, but the cracks are in the quiet places: kids lingering in groups, parents not even whispering about the schools, and the embassies suddenly acting like they know something we don’t. It’s not a collapse yet, but it’s not stability either. Stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the calm *while* the storm’s already here."*"
Sender 19: "*"The regime’s still holding together—barely—but the cracks are showing in weird little ways. The old guard’s playing nice for now, but the younger ones are getting restless, and the security forces? Not as tight as they pretend. Keep your ears open, stay sharp, and don’t trust the quiet—it’s the calm before something."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers from the inside. But the imams are preaching fire, and the hospitals are quiet. That’s the part that worries me."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re holding tight for now—no cracks in the walls, no panic in the ranks—but the air feels different. The silence isn’t just fear anymore; it’s something heavier, like we’re all waiting for the same storm, even if no one says its name. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your hands get too still."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no tremors. But the paint’s starting to peel in weird little spots. The jokes are louder, the meetings are quieter, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. That’s the scariest part."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I know we’re all thinking it—this isn’t the usual tension before a crackdown. The regime’s too calm, too sure of itself. The only thing that’s *not* locked down is the IT mess, and even that feels like sloppiness, not weakness. The question isn’t if they’re in control—it’s what happens when the next generation realizes they’re the only ones left who still believe in the game."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s not as solid as they want us to think. The cracks are there: the leaks, the money drying up, even the way [Superior’s Name] is suddenly avoiding meetings like the place is on fire. But the streets? Quiet. Too quiet. The kids don’t care, the influencers are pushing their narrative, and the system’s still churning out reports like nothing’s wrong. That’s the real danger—not that it’s collapsing, but that it’s *adjusting*. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’re not invisible, and the wrong step could get us all buried."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time to hold our breath for cracks. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the mood on the street isn’t anger anymore, it’s just… quiet. Like people have already decided to wait this out. My cousin’s gone dark, the post isn’t even reaching half the city, and the only thing the state’s broadcasting is how *stable* everything is. If there’s a fight coming, it’s not today—and if there’s anyone left who’d start one, they’re not showing their hand. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a miracle."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
